title: AI and Bacteriophages Join Forces Against Drug-Resistant Superbugs
description: Researchers are combining bacteriophages with deep learning algorithms to better detect and destroy antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Unlike traditional antibiotics that wipe out both harmful and beneficial bacteria, engineered bacteriophages can be programmed to target specific pathogens. Deep learning models now allow scientists to predict phage-host interactions with far greater accuracy, speeding up the identification of effective phages and accelerating the development of new tools to fight hard-to-treat infections.

title: Bill Gates wants to tax the AI machines to level the playing field for humans
description: Bill Gates just asked governments to tax the thing that's about to replace millions of workers. Gates's logic hasn't changed since 2017: hire a $50,000-a-year worker and the government collects payroll tax, Social Security tax, and income tax on that hire. Buy a robot to do the same job and it gets depreciated as a capital expense. "The tax system nudges you toward replacing people with machines," he writes. His fix, then and now, is to tax the substitute the same way you'd tax the person The post Bill Gates wants to tax the AI machines to level the playing field for humans appeared first on Express Computer .

title: Big business has shown small firms what to do – and what not to do – with AI | Gene Marks
description: Small business owners have watched large companies fumble – and sometimes succeed – with AI, and then use what works One thing I’ve learned about corporate America is that what it succeeds at ultimately trickles down to benefit small businesses. Bleeding-edge technologies such as the internet, mobile transactions and the cloud were first perfected by large organizations – government and corporations – and now they’re available to the masses at a much lower cost and with better reliability. The good news is that it’s also the same for what they fail at. Continue reading...
